newsitem.title: CANADA: Fletcher Canada sees firmer pulp, paper.
newsitem.headline: Fletcher Canada sees firmer pulp, paper.

text.p: Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd, which reported on Tuesday a C$14.2 million loss for its fiscal third quarter, said it anticipated stronger pulp and paper markets over the rest of 1997.

"The prospects for strengthening paper markets through the remainder of 1997 are favorable," Chief Executive Doug Whitehead said in a statement. The loss in the third quarter translated to C$0.11 a share.
The pulp and paper maker is majority owned by New Zealand's Fletcher Challenge Ltd.
Fletcher blamed the loss for the third quarter ended March 31 on "very difficult cold weather operating conditions early in the quarter and market-related downtime."
"Markets, after slowing dramatically in early 1996, have only recently begun to show signs of improvement," it said.
But Whitehead said paper consumption had been increasing since late 1996, "bringing improved balance to markets for newsprint and lightweight coated paper toward the end of the quarter."
"...The trend in consumption is positive and the pricing environment is now improving," he added.
Paper shipments fell in the third quarter over the prior quarter, so Fletcher curtailed production by 24,000 tonnes.

Fletcher said pulp markets weakened in the quarter because of excess production and a rise in producer inventories in January and February. Producer inventories declined in March, but finished the quarter above levels of three months earlier, Fletcher said.
The company cut its pulp production by about 13,000 tonnes in the quarter.
